excerpts.content:
Today if I created a transaction with a `gasPrice` of `1000 nanoeth per gas` I would pay `1000 nanoeth per gas` even if `10 nanoeth per gas` would have gotten me included in the block.

After 1559 if you set your `fee_cap` to `1000 nanoeth per gas` and your `miner_fee` to `1 nanoeth per gas` and the `base_fee` of the block you are included in ends up being `9 nanoeth per gas` then you'll pay `10 nanoeth per gas`.

excerpts.author: nickjohnson
excerpts.content: Yes, but the system is designed to adjust so that the demand for blockspace at the current base fee is equal to the supply.

excerpts.author: nickjohnson
excerpts.content: When demand is relatively stable, that means you can have a statically-set tip and just pay that.

excerpts.author: nickjohnson
excerpts.content: When demand is spiking it degrades to a first-price auction like the current system until the feedback mechanism catches up.

excerpts.author: nickjohnson
excerpts.content: Overpaying by large amounts is fairly uncommon while demand is stable, though!

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: And when demand isn't stable people get frustrated with stuck transactions.  🙂

excerpts.author: nickjohnson
excerpts.content: (Worth noting - if you have a particularly large TX, you usually have to bump your gas price to ensure it gets included early in the block. This is likely to still be the case with miner tips under 1559.)

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: If you haven't read my blog post linked above I encourage you to do so, it goes over the UX problem users currently face and why 1559 fixes it.  A bit long though.

excerpts.author: nickjohnson
excerpts.content: Although as long as they set the cap high enough, at least their TX will make it in when demand stops increasing, rather than having to wait for the price to drop or resubmit.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: This is critical.

excerpts.author: cakez1r2648
excerpts.content: I see. That makes sense. I did read your post, Micah. Thank you

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: The assumption I am making is that people will behave rationally and set their `max_fee` to the max they are *willing* to pay, and the assumption that in many (most?) cases that is substantially above the current `base_fee`.

excerpts.author: cakez1r2648
excerpts.content: This is the part I was missing in my understanding. I hadn't figured that out

excerpts.author: nickjohnson
excerpts.content: That seems optimistic 😆

excerpts.author: nickjohnson
excerpts.content: (It's also a UX challenge to make that a meaningful choice available to users, I'd say)
